key_figures: Harbormaster Ilsa Vane — takes bribes in fresh water, which is worth more than gold since the wells went brackish.
Sahuagin defector called Ssketh — begs sanctuary in a rain barrel, claims the Deep Maw is eating its own priest caste.
Tidecaller Wren — a drowned-god priestess who reads the future in flotsam; her prophecies always cost someone a finger.
Captain Harlow — smuggler queen of the Drowned Rat; runs blackwater gin and escaped debtors through the reef at night.
The Salt Abbess — runs a hospice where the dying are pickled alive "for the lean years"; half the city fears her, half owes her.
Bosun Cobb — lost his crew to sahuagin nets, now hires landsmen for "revenge voyages" that never return.
Mirella the Eel — fence for drowned jewelry; can tell which corpses wore it by smell alone.
Father Drown — street preacher who baptizes converts by holding them under harbor water until they stop struggling.
Scribe Pell — keeps the official drowning registry; for a fee, the drowned stay "alive" and their widows keep the pensions.
Knife-Jaw Joren — pit fighter with sahuagin teeth sewn into his gums; undefeated, possibly no longer entirely human.
The Lamplighter — tends the reef beacons; the only man the sahuagin won't take, and nobody knows why.
Widow Salt — brewes brine-poison for assassinations; each batch named after the husband it avenged.
Quartermaster Voss — sells imperial weapons out the back of the garrison; checks every coin by biting it twice.
Little Fen — nine-year-old pickpocket who claims she can hold her breath for an hour; the guild is testing the claim.
Anatomist Dr. Morwain — pays in silver for sahuagin corpses, in gold for live ones; her cellar stairs go down past the waterline.
Chaplain Brack — garrison priest who blesses the tide-gates each dawn; the one morning he slept late, the east gate drowned.
Sahuagin brood-tender Hysh — captured egg-guardian; sings to an empty tank and refuses all food but live crabs.
Ropemaker Tam — his nooses never rot; every gallows rope in the city is his work, and he measures necks for free.
The Drowned Rat's cook, Stove — feeds the crew things pulled from nets that no menu names; the crew has stopped asking.
Toll-keeper Agda — exacts the bridge toll in teeth since coin ran short; wears the defaults on a necklace.
Cartographer Ilya — maps the streets that only exist at low tide; three of her maps show a cathedral nobody built.
Bellfounder Orm — casting a bell meant to be heard underwater; the foundry works nights and the neighbors have moved.
Leechwife Nessa — her leeches refuse noble blood but gorge on sailors; she charges accordingly and keeps no records.
Deserter Corvin — imperial marine who swam away from a sahuagin boarding action; the Empire lists him drowned, the sahuagin list him property.
The Cistern King — rules the freshwater black market from the old reservoir; executes thieves by thirst, not hanging.
Gull-tongue Paz — interpreter who claims fluency in sahuagin clicks; both sides suspect she invents the translations for profit.
Shipbreaker Hedd — dismantles quarantined hulls plank by plank; wears a dead ship's bell as a helmet and answers to it.
Novice Sarella — fled the Salt Abbey with the pickling ledgers; half the hospice's "dead" are listed as inventory, alive.
Wreck-diver Sim — free-dives the sunken cathedral for relics; came up last week speaking a language his mother understands.
The Maw's Voice — a sahuagin priest broadcasting surrender terms through a drowned choir of captives; the terms get worse weekly.
Mother Cask — runs the floating creche lashed to the quarantine hulks; the children are indentured out by the inch of their height.
The Assayer — tastes the drowned for the probate court; claims the dead taste sweeter after a storm and bills accordingly.
Half-Bell Tomas — a diver who came up halved; swears his other half is still down there, knocking.
Lady Brine — drowned noble who holds court in a flooded ballroom; her guests never notice they are dead, and she never tells them.
The Chainwright — forges chains the sahuagin will not touch; prices his work in childhood memories, taken on delivery.
Patchwork Ivo — a gallows-bridge surgeon who sews back what the tide takes, and sometimes what it returns instead.
Sable Fen — night-market fence for the Choir's stolen song-sheets; every sheet she sells is one voice fewer in the surrender chorus.
The Tide Notary — registers every legal drowning; no witness who signs his ledger has ever been seen above water afterward.
Gristle Ann — pie-woman of the Eel Market whose fillings are named, daily, after the recently missing.
Dockfather Munn — eldest of the longshore; his word is law until the second bell, and the second bell always comes.
Corrosion Sal — a chemist-witch who dissolves anything for anyone and keeps the residue of every job.
Envoy Prill — imperial envoy to a drowned court; fluent in etiquette, deaf to warnings, dry in a city that is not.
Blackline — a cartographer's apprentice who inked Ilya's cathedral map and now cannot stop drawing the sea over everything.
The Hulk's Parson — preaches to the quarantine hulls at dusk; the congregations knock back in time with the psalms.
Ninepenny Nell — children's moneylender; the collateral is baby teeth, and Agda's toll-house enforces collection.
Sluice — a tide-gate engineer who knows which of Chaplain Brack's blessings are load-bearing, and sells the list in pieces.
Apprentice Vail — last student of a brinecaller who dissolved mid-invocation; the invocation is still running, through him.
Griselda Toome — auditor of the Salt Abbey's pickling accounts; the inventory lists her twice and she has only caught one.
The Reef's Tooth — half-sahuagin sellsword brokering reef passage; takes payment in ears and gives directions honestly.
Longwake Oda — a helmswoman who has not slept in eleven years because her dreams drown other people instead of her.
Candlepin — a chandler who pours funeral candles; every wick he lights is seen walking somewhere in the city that night.
Cellarer Grub — keeps the Drowned Rat's gin vaults and one locked cask he answers to by name, and the name is not his.
Sister Salt-Marrow — Brine Sister infirmarian who sheltered Sarella and wrote a confession about it, then hid the confession.
Harrowgate — an imperial deserter-hunter pursuing Corvin under a writ that outlived the empire that issued it.
The Tideglass Keeper — tends the harbor tideglass; when the sand runs up, he walks to the black beacon, and will not say why.
Mirefoot — a bog-guide through the drowned tenements; navigates by sound because the silt shows nothing and takes everything.
Aunt Billow — a retired storm-caller with a rooftop garden whose roses all taste, faintly, of wreck.
Quiet Rafe — a mute courier of the Blackwater Compact; carries messages no one speaks aloud and delivers every one.
Brother Quill — the Salt Abbess's almoner; dispenses hospice charity and logs each recipient in the inventory ledgers.
Vess — sahuagin hunt-priestess sent to recover the defector Ssketh; speaks flawless, cruel Common and worse silence.
places: The Rotting Pier — lower docks built on drowned tenements; at low tide you can hear the old city through the planks.
The Brine Chapel — salt-stained chapel in the pier pilings where Tidecaller Wren reads flotsam; entry costs a secret.
The Drowned Rat (tavern) — smugglers' den in a half-sunk hulk; the floor tilts with the tide and so do the deals.
The Salt Abbey hospice — whitewashed walls, vinegar smell, and ledgers that list the living as stores.
The Old Reservoir — freshwater fortress of the Cistern King; the last clean water in the city, guarded by the thirsty.
The Reef Beacons — lamplighter-tended lights marking the safe channel; one beacon shines black at new moon.
The Gallows Bridge — Agda's toll bridge; the railings are hung with the teeth of those who couldn't pay.
Morwain's Cellar — anatomist's surgery below the waterline; the tanks breathe when the tide comes in.
The Sunken Cathedral — visible only at lowest tide; Sim dives it, and something down there has started diving back.
The Garrison Tide-Gates — imperial engineering holding back the harbor; Chaplain Brack's blessing is load-bearing.
The Eel Market — Mirella's fencing stalls among the fish guts; everything for sale was worn by someone first.
The Quarantine Hulks — Hedd's shipbreaking yard of plague ships; the quarantine flags never come down, by design.
The Drowned Court — Lady Brine's flooded ballroom; invitations float, and the tide seats the guests.
The Night Market Stairs — under the Eel Market, wading-deep at high water, where song-sheets change hands without words.
The Floating Creche — Mother Cask's lashed-hulk orphanage, listing permanently a few degrees toward the sea.
The Tidegate Engine Room — Sluice's domain of ropes and relic-plaques; the blessing plates are load-bearing and loose.
The Assay House — where the Assayer tastes the dead for the probate court; the queue is alive, the service window is not.
Gallowsmarket — the stalls beneath the bridge; rent is paid to Agda in teeth and sublet in secrets.
The Brackish Stairs — the water-stair to the Cistern King's reservoir; petitioners are counted going down and going up, and the numbers differ.
The Bellfoundry Yards — Orm's night works; the molds are shaped for a sound no air bell has ever made.
The Imperial Chancery, drowned wing — Envoy Prill's office, knee-deep in protocol and brine, the seals still dry somehow.
Mother Cask's Landing — the jetty where the creche rowboat ties up empty at dusk and leaves full at dark.
The Wet Archive — the city's drowning registers in a weeping stone vault; Pell's back room, where the dead stay alive on paper.
The Black Beacon — the second reef light, unlit for a generation; the Tideglass Keeper walks there whenever the sand runs up.
factions: The Blackwater Compact — Harlow's smuggler syndicate; owns the night reef and rents to anyone the Empire won't.
The Drowned Choir — the Maw's Voice's captive congregation; sings the surrender terms whether it wills or no.
The Brine Sisters — Salt Abbess's hospice order; pickles, prays, and keeps the inventory ledgers Sarella stole.
The Imperial Garrison — holds the tide-gates and the bridge; underpaid, undermanned, and selling its own armory.
The Freshwater Trust — Cistern King's monopoly; water is currency, thirst is enforcement.
The Lowtide Guild — Fen's pickpockets and Ilya's cartographers; maps what the tide uncovers, steals what it leaves.
The Reefwardens — the Lamplighter's old order, down to one man; keeps lights the city stopped paying for.
The Deep Maw's Brood — sahuagin priest caste pressing from below; even its defectors fear what it has become.
The Probate Court of Drownings — tastes the dead and divides estates; the Assayer is its tongue and its appetite.
The Longshore Assembly — Dockfather Munn's guild; the law until the second bell, and a strike is only ever rumored.
The Choir's Silence — a splinter congregation escaped from the Drowned Choir; they sing nothing, defiantly, and the sea notices.
The Water-Barons — the Cistern King's enforcers; hold thirst as a writ and water as a verdict.
The Night Foundry Hands — Orm's bell-casters, sworn to finish the casting before the sea finishes the city.
The Gallowsmarket Tenants — the bridge stall-holders; their rent-roll circulates as a second currency beneath Agda's teeth.
The Hull-Speakers — parsons and divers who commune with the quarantine hulks; they answer the knocking, and keep logs.
The Empire's Patience — imperial loyalists waiting for a relief fleet the tide has likely already eaten.
notes: The sunken cathedral has begun answering Bellfounder Orm's underwater bell on the lowest tides, and the Gallows Bridge rings with it in time, Agda's teeth chattering on their necklace. Wreck-diver Sim has surfaced for the last time, speaking only the language his mother understands, and the Maw's Voice has stopped broadcasting surrender terms: the Drowned Choir now sings only numbers — the city's living, counted, fewer each week. The Cistern King is level 18, the apex of the water-barons, and the Freshwater Trust enforces his word as an archmage of thirst would; Brother Quill has begun copying the inventory ledgers Sarella stole, and Sister Salt-Marrow's confession names everyone who knew. Vess the hunt-priestess is ashore and asking Harrowgate's writ questions. New subjects for this build: the Tollhouse of Teeth, Agda's counting-house on the bridge; the Pale Ledger, a book that rewrites the city's debts overnight and is kept in the Wet Archive; the Tideglass, an instrument that runs upward on drowning nights; and the Brackish Herald, a drowned-god envoy asking after the fate of a hulk called the Rusting Hulk.
